extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants and reviewers (particularly SBIR/STTR Phase I applicants)
extracted.subtask_short: NIH SBIR Phase I peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Summary statement and reviewer critique for an NIH SBIR (R43) Phase I application, using standard NIH peer review criteria to evaluate scientific merit and administrative/compliance items. It records criterion scores, strengths/weaknesses, and committee recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project address an important problem or critical barrier in the field? Will successful completion of the aims change the concepts, methods, technologies, treatments, services, or preventative interventions that drive the field?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strength examples from reviewers: "Improved structural insight into antibody:antigen binding epitopes will have significant benefits"; "The increased speed ... will enable determination earlier in drug discovery". Weakness example: reviewer noted "None that are apparent" when no weakness identified. Use preliminary data and a strong scientific premise to support significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the PD(s)/PI(s), collaborators, and other researchers well suited to the project? Do they have the appropriate experience, training, and complementary expertise to carry out the work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strength examples: "Investigators are leaders in development and application of multiplex SPR...basic biology of HSV...computational modeling"; "unique collection of expertise"; evidence of productive interactions (e.g., embedded company employee). Weakness example: none identified. Emphasize multidisciplinary, complementary expertise and demonstrated collaborative history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the application challenge and seek to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms by using novel theoretical concepts, approaches, methodologies, or technologies?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer strengths: "Combining the multiplexed experimental technique (SPR) with computational modeling ... is novel." and "designing mutations based on prior knowledge and modeling to evaluate putative binding modes is interesting." Weakness example: lack of survey of existing related methods can weaken the claim of novelty. Show how your approach differs from existing methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the overall strategy, methodology, and analyses well-reasoned and appropriate to accomplish the specific aims? Are potential problems, alternative strategies, and benchmarks for success presented?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strength examples: "Clearly articulated aims with alternatives; investigators articulate potential risks and pitfalls and provide alternatives"; "fit-for-purpose approach focusing on residue-level info rather than atomic resolution". Weakness examples noted across reviewers: lack of details around metrics to assess clustering accuracy; lack of detailed description of measures for assessing performance of epitope identification; unclear statistical metrics and lack of baseline comparison. Guidance: include clear metrics, statistical methods, and baseline/comparator approaches; describe computational methods in sufficient detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the scientific environment in which the work will be done contribute to the probability of success? Are institutional support, equipment, and other resources available?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strength examples: cross-disciplinary, cross-institution effort; combined resources of company and universities (microfluidics, SPR imagers, cell/tissue culture, FACS, computation). Weakness example: none identified. Emphasize available infrastructure and institutional support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact (Priority Score)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewers' assessment of the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved. Committee assigns an overall impact score (1-9) and an impact/priority score is calculated for reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text guidance: "The impact/priority score is calculated after discussion of an application by averaging the overall scores (1-9) given by all voting reviewers on the committee and multiplying by 10." Reviewers' written critiques inform the overall impact; strengths/weaknesses in Significance, Investigators, Innovation, Approach, and Environment influence this judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion scoring mechanics and reviewer submission practice
rubrics_metrics.description: How criterion and overall scores are handled and reported in NIH review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion scores (Significance, Investigator(s), Innovation, Approach, Environment) are submitted prior to the meeting by individual assigned reviewers and are not discussed specifically at the review meeting or calculated into the overall impact score. The overall impact score is calculated after discussion by averaging overall scores and multiplying by 10. Some applications may also receive a percentile ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the adequacy of protections for human subjects if applicable to the work (or Not Applicable if no human subjects involved).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For this application: "Not Applicable (No Human Subjects)". When applicable, reviewers expect a clear plan describing protections, consent, and regulatory compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of proposed use of live vertebrate animals (or Not Applicable if none proposed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For this application: "Not Applicable (No Vertebrate Animals)". If animals are used, reviewers expect justification, welfare considerations, and appropriate oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of biological hazardous materials and safety protections (or Not Applicable if none).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For this application: "Not Applicable (No Biohazards)". If biohazards are present, include containment, training, and institutional approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan and documentation for authentication of key biological and chemical reagents and resources used in the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This application received an "Unacceptable" rating for this item: "The investigators will use a collection of HSV reagents including gD variants. This reviewer was unable to find a discussion of the authentication of these reagents." Guidance: provide a clear plan for authentication (source, validation, tracking) of critical reagents to avoid unacceptable ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support (including compliance with caps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the requested budget and justification for the period of support, including compliance with program/solicitation caps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee noted the amount requested is reasonable but the budget is over the mandatory cap and was not justified as required. Guidance to applicant: explicitly discuss why the proposed costs exceed any programmatic hard cap and justify that those costs are necessary for the Phase I aims. Committee Budget Recommendations may adjust final award calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosketch Format Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance of investigator biosketches with NIH-required format and policy changes (e.g., NOT-OD-15-032).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific Review Officer's note: during review one or more biosketches did not comply with the required format. Applicants must review the policy and ensure biosketches comply; NIH may withdraw noncompliant applications from review or consideration for funding.
